mechanism: Ketorolac (NSAID) reduces renal blood flow and can impair renal function, while oxybutynin has anticholinergic effects that may reduce urine output; combined effect increases risk of urinary retention and acute kidney injury.
action: Monitor renal function, urinary output, and fluid status; consider alternative analgesic or anticholinergic agent; ensure adequate hydration and assess for urinary retention.
